newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin says can block some, not all, NATO plans.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin says can block some, not all, NATO plans.

text.p: Moscow will have a "deciding vote" in NATO decisions affecting Russia but not in internal affairs of the Western defence pact under a treaty agreed this week, the Kremlin's chief spokesman was quoted as saying on Saturday.

"There are issues of NATO's inner life, there are issues connected to the activities of NATO as an organisation to which Russia does not belong. Those are NATO's domestic goings on," Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency.

"As for the sphere of joint activity -- and these are stipulated in the document to be signed in Paris -- of the mutual interests of Russia and NATO, of the areas where Russia can play the role of partner, then here Russia will have a deciding vote."

Yastrzhembsky, who is also a foreign affairs adviser to President Boris Yeltsin, was commenting on the apparent contradiction between remarks made by the Kremlin leader and U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday, when Russian and NATO negotiators finally agreed a deal on a new relationship.
Yeltsin said: "Decisions can be taken only by consensus. If Russia is against some decision, it means this decision will not go through."
Clinton said: "Russia will work closely with NATO but not in NATO, giving Russia a voice but not a veto over NATO's business."

Western officials have explained the apparent discrepancy in the same way as Yastrzhembsky. A permanent joint NATO-Russia council will give Moscow a say in matters affecting it, but not on other affairs of the alliance.
Yeltsin, concerned about Russian security and the reaction of nationalist opponents at home, has fiercely opposed NATO's plan to admit former Soviet-bloc states in eastern Europe.
But he said the new treaty, to be signed in Paris on May 27, has persuaded him that future relations with Moscow's old Cold War adversary can be peaceful.
